title: Format Specifiers
objective: Control how a value is displayed inside an f-string using a format specifier.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Full Course for free
sourceAlignment.creator: Bro Code
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; this topic isn't covered in Python Crash Course but is taught in the companion video. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Inside an f-string, you can add a format specifier after a colon to control exactly how a value is displayed, without changing the value itself. f"{price:.2f}" always shows price with exactly two digits after the decimal point, even if the real number has more or fewer.
.2f means 'fixed-point, 2 digits after the decimal' — the f stands for fixed-point notation, and the number before it sets how many decimal digits to show, rounding if there are more.

Format specifiers can also pad numbers with leading zeros: f"{minutes:02}" shows minutes as at least two digits, adding a leading zero if it's a single digit — 5 becomes 05, but 12 stays 12. This is common when displaying something like a clock.
explanation.rule: Add :spec after a value inside an f-string's curly braces to control its display — .2f for two decimal places, 02 for zero-padded width.

examples.title: Rounding to Two Decimals
examples.note: 19.5 becomes 19.50 — .2f always shows exactly two digits after the decimal point.

examples.title: Zero-Padding a Clock
examples.note: Both numbers are padded to at least two digits, so the display reads 05:09 instead of 5:9.

feedback.correct: Correct — .2f always shows exactly two digits after the decimal point, even for a whole number.
feedback.incorrect: .2f forces exactly two decimal digits to be shown, padding with zeros if needed.

assignment.title: Forge Timer Display
assignment.brief: Write timer_display(minutes, seconds) that returns a string formatted as MM:SS, zero-padding each part to two digits.
requirements: Use the :02 format specifier on both minutes and seconds inside an f-string.
Return the formatted string in the form MM:SS.
assignment.starterCode:
def timer_display(minutes, seconds):
    # Return an MM:SS string, zero-padding each part to two digits.
    pass

print(timer_display(5, 9))
print(timer_display(12, 3))
assignment.solutionCode:
def timer_display(minutes, seconds):
    return f"{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}"

print(timer_display(5, 9))
print(timer_display(12, 3))

hints: f"{minutes:02}" pads minutes to at least two digits with a leading zero.
The same :02 pattern works for seconds too.
Join them with a colon inside one f-string: f"{minutes:02}:{seconds:02}".
